SMTO-SKL-0165 — GitHub asked SMTO to slow down

GUID: c40f3729-4ab0-5749-90a3-c91fdfe3474b
Slug: github-secondary-rate-limited
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • GitHub saw too many requests in a short time and asked SMTO to pause, even though your overall allowance may not be used up. GitHub refused this request, so nothing changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait at least one minute. If SMTO reported a longer wait for this step, wait that long instead. GitHub refuses requests from this account until the pause is over.
  2. Repeat your request, asking for one thing at a time instead of many GitHub actions together. This kind of limit is triggered by bursts of requests, not by your total use.

What success looks like

  • After the pause, your request completes without a slow-down message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't switch tokens to avoid the pause, and don't send the same change several times.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GitHub returned 403/429 with rate-limit signals but remaining requests were not zero, so SMTO classified a secondary rate limit and set a cooldown of at least 60 seconds or the Retry-After value.

What this means

  • HTTP 403/429 has rate-limit evidence without a zero remaining count, producing the secondary-limit classification and a bounded cooldown. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • HTTP 403/429 has rate-limit evidence without a zero remaining count, producing the secondary-limit classification and a bounded cooldown.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect Retry-After and the secondary-limit evidence rather than switching tokens.

How to fix it

  • GitHubClient.error classifies secondary_rate_limited and records a per-token cooldown of max(60 s, Retry-After). Stop requests for retry_after, reduce request frequency and concurrency, and repeat reads only after the delay; throttled writes are never retried automatically.
  • Stop requests for retry_after (at least GitHub's secondary-limit guidance). Reduce request frequency and retry only reads after the delay.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Subsequent permitted reads respect the recorded cooldown and reduced frequency.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
